name: Communications Management Plan
one_liner: Who gets told what, by whom, how often and in what form — meeting by meeting, report by report.
purpose: The Communications Management Plan helps to ensure that all project stakeholders have the information they need to perform their roles throughout the project. It defines and documents communication activities, their goals, content, format, frequency and audience. It also defines how project status and the assignment of activities are communicated, and includes a communication strategy for each key stakeholder based on their interests, expectations and influence in the project.

fields.what: All approvers are required and records of each must be kept; listed reviewers are required unless explicitly marked Optional.
fields.who: PM drafts · PO approves · BM supports
fields.castor: Approve: Florence Nightingale (PO). Review: Grace Hopper (BM), Henry Gantt (PSO).

fields.what: Revision, date, created by and short description of changes, latest version first; editorial and clarification edits need no re-approval.
fields.castor: v0.4 20 May 2026 stakeholder review · v1.0 26 Jun 2026 approved with the Handbook baseline.

fields.what: Where the latest controlled version of this plan is stored, so every stakeholder reads the same version.
fields.castor: CASTOR repository, 02 Planning; filed as 16.Communications_Management_Plan.CASTOR.26-06-2026.v1.0.docx.

fields.what: States that the plan determines how to communicate most efficiently to the various stakeholders, defining content, format, frequency, audience and expected results.
fields.castor: Covers ESM internal audiences plus Levallois Systems as contractor; no external/press communication in scope.

fields.what: For each key stakeholder, the strategy based on their interests, expectations and influence — what they need, why, and what result is expected.
fields.who: PM defines from the Stakeholder Matrix · BM assists
fields.castor: Lorenzo de' Medici (AGB) receives portfolio-level Progress Reports only; Marie Curie (UR) gets hands-on release walkthroughs.

fields.what: Communication must be adequate, specific, sufficient, concise and timely, and must manage expectations on progress, quality reporting and activity assignment.
fields.castor: One-page Status Report monthly; Florence Nightingale explicitly asked for business impact, not technical detail.

fields.what: The Stakeholder Matrix is the major input for identifying stakeholder groups; Project Charter, Project Handbook with related plans, and Project Work Plan supply the content.
fields.castor: CASTOR Stakeholder Matrix groups: Lending Operations, Finance & Control, Risk, Legal, IT & Digital, Levallois.

fields.what: The media used — emails, documents, phone calls, meetings — and the artefacts that carry or support them, such as MoMs, reports, logs and the repository.
fields.castor: Meetings at ESM Kirchberg with video for Levallois; artefacts in MS-Word in the project repository.

fields.what: Why the meeting exists and what must be true after it; for the Planning Kick-off, scope, governance, roles and risks must all be clear.
fields.castor: Planning Kick-off, 09 Apr 2026: agree CASTOR scope, governance and first risk set before planning starts.

fields.what: Where the meeting is held; often 'defined by the Project Manager in time' for kick-offs, or by the Project Owner for PSC meetings.
fields.castor: ESM, Luxembourg City (Kirchberg), with video for Gustave Eiffel and remote Levallois staff.

fields.what: How often: once per project for kick-offs, monthly for the PSC (or when a milestone needs approval), bi-annually or annually for Project Review Meetings.
fields.castor: PSC monthly · Status Meeting weekly · PCT Meeting weekly · Change Control Meeting fortnightly.

fields.what: Who chairs. PM chairs kick-offs, Status, Review, Change Control and Project-End Review; the PO chairs the PSC; the Team Leader chairs the PCT Meeting.
fields.who: Set in the plan, not improvised
fields.castor: PSC chaired by Florence Nightingale (PO); all other CASTOR meetings chaired by the PM.

fields.what: Who takes the minutes: BM for the PSC Meeting, Project Support Officer for the Project Review Meeting, Team Leader for the PCT Meeting; others as the PM defines.
fields.who: Named in the plan before the meeting
fields.castor: PSC minutes by Grace Hopper (BM); Project Review minutes by Henry Gantt (PSO).

fields.what: The required and optional participants, by role. Kick-offs include PO, BM, SP, PM, PCT, BIG and URs; the PSC is PO, SP, BM, PM plus optional roles.
fields.who: PM invites · roles taken from the Stakeholder Matrix
fields.castor: PSC: Florence Nightingale, Leonardo da Vinci, Grace Hopper, PM, Marie Curie (UR), Albert Einstein (AO).

fields.what: The standing agenda for that meeting type, reused each time; the Meeting Agenda template turns it into a dated, timed agenda.
fields.who: Chairperson owns · PM issues in advance
fields.castor: PSC standing items: debriefing, problems and actions, scope/budget/finish-date status, formal approvals.

fields.what: Who receives the minutes — usually all invited participants; for PCT Meetings also the PM, who consolidates sub-project minutes.
fields.castor: PSC minutes to all PSC members plus Lorenzo de' Medici (AGB) for information only.

fields.what: What the meeting produces and in what form: MS-Word minutes by email, updated Decision Log, updated Change Log, Status or Progress Report.
fields.who: Minute-taker produces · PM ensures logs updated
fields.castor: PSC output: MoM in MS-Word by email plus a Decision Log update the same day.

fields.what: What each report conveys. Status Report is a one-pager with traffic lights; the Progress Report is a fuller overview; the Quality Review Report covers quality findings.
fields.castor: CASTOR Status Report traffic-lights cost, schedule, scope/changes, risks and issues on one page.

fields.what: Status Report follows the Project Status Meeting; Progress Report follows the Project Review Meeting; Project-End Report is produced once in Closing.
fields.castor: Status Report monthly; Progress Report bi-annually; Project-End Report once, ahead of 12 Jul 2028.

fields.what: Who writes it. The PM authors all reports except the Outsourcing (Contractor) Status Report, written by the contractor's project manager.
fields.who: PM · contractor's PM for the outsourcing report
fields.castor: Contractor Status Report authored by Gustave Eiffel (Levallois CPM); summarised by the PM in the Status Report.

fields.f: Report block — Distributed to / Media / Reference to
fields.what: The audience (often 'refer to the related meeting'), the format (Word document), and a link to the actual document instance.
fields.castor: Quality Review Report to the PSC and W. Edwards Deming (PQA); Word document in 04 Monitor & Control.

fields.what: One block per other regular communication item: name, description, audience, frequency, media — for anything not a standard meeting or report.
fields.castor: Monthly CASTOR newsletter to the 40 loan administrators affected by the transition; owner Grace Hopper.

fields.what: One-page consolidation: Item Name, Audience (summary), Responsible person, Frequency, Media of Communication — one row per meeting and per report.
fields.castor: Thirteen rows: eight CASTOR meetings, five reports; responsible person is the PM except the contractor report.

fields.what: ID, reference or related document, and source or link/location — title, version, date and source for each referenced artefact.
fields.castor: References 04 Project Handbook, 05 Project Stakeholder Matrix and the CASTOR project folder.

traps: Approved by the PO (A); the PSC is only Informed — unlike the Quality Management Plan.
BM is Supports (S) here, one of the few S cells in the Planning RASCI.
PSC Meeting is chaired by the PO and minuted by the BM — not the PM.
The Stakeholder Matrix is an input to this plan, not a section of it.
MoM items — issues, risks, decisions, changes — must also be recorded in the relevant logs.
